meta.title: Chef Lucy's Egg Fried Rice
meta.textType: functional: a recipe and a short talk, a blog post

paragraphs: Posted by Lily. On Saturday, December nineteenth, the Explorers went to a cooking class. Teacher Kim read the directions from a map. "Walk along the main street." "Turn right at the bookshop." "The cooking class is the third door past the cafe." We walked from the bus stop and found the door. Chef Lucy gave us white aprons. Then she gave a short talk with three rules. "First, wash your hands." "Second, use a spoon to taste." "Third, if you want to use the stove, ask me first." On the wall hung a card, "EGG FRIED RICE, for six."

First, we had to prepare the ingredients. "Would you cut the mushrooms, Mia?" asked Chef Lucy. Mia cut them on a board with a small knife. Chef Lucy watched her hands. May beat four eggs in a bowl with a fork. "Would you pass the salt, please, Leo?" asked May. Leo put the salt next to the bowl. Then May added a little pepper.

Chef Lucy fried the rice, and the kitchen smelled good. She put the rice on six plates. Then she put a thin slice of chili on top of each plate. We sat down at a big table and ate the dish. It was tasty, but the chili was hot. Leo held up his spoon and grinned. "Cooking is easier than homework," he said. Teacher Kim laughed and took more rice. Chef Lucy smiled.

Here is our recipe for six people. You need three cups of cooked rice, four eggs, and six mushrooms. You also need three cloves of garlic, one small chili, three spoons of oil, salt, and pepper. Step one: wash your hands. Step two: cut the mushrooms and the garlic. Step three: mix the eggs with a little salt and pepper. Step four: heat the oil in a pan. Step five: fry the rice, the garlic, and the mushrooms. Step six: add the eggs and mix, and put a slice of chili on top.

"How much oil do we need?" I asked Chef Lucy. "Three spoons," she said. "How many people can eat this dish?" asked Mia. "Six," said Chef Lucy, "and the recipe is easy." Would you cook this dish at home? Please ask an adult before you use the stove. Tell us in a message how it tasted!
text.summary: Lily writes a blog post about the Explorers' visit to Chef Lucy's cooking class. It tells the way there, the three rules, the cooking, and the recipe for egg fried rice.

Teacher Kim read the directions from a map.
"Walk along the main street."
"Turn right at the bookshop."
"The cooking class is the third door past the cafe."
We walked from the bus stop and found the door.
Chef Lucy gave us white aprons.
Then she gave a short talk with three rules.
"First, wash your hands."
"Second, use a spoon to taste."
"Third, if you want to use the stove, ask me first."
On the wall hung a card, "EGG FRIED RICE, for six."
First, we had to prepare the ingredients.
"Would you cut the mushrooms, Mia?" asked Chef Lucy.
Mia cut them on a board with a small knife.
Chef Lucy watched her hands.
May beat four eggs in a bowl with a fork.
"Would you pass the salt, please, Leo?" asked May.
Leo put the salt next to the bowl.
Then May added a little pepper.
Chef Lucy fried the rice, and the kitchen smelled good.
She put the rice on six plates.
Then she put a thin slice of chili on top of each plate.
We sat down at a big table and ate the dish.
It was tasty, but the chili was hot.
Leo held up his spoon and grinned.
"Cooking is easier than homework," he said.
Teacher Kim laughed and took more rice.
Chef Lucy smiled.
Here is our recipe for six people.
You need three cups of cooked rice, four eggs, and six mushrooms.
You also need three cloves of garlic, one small chili, three spoons of oil, salt, and pepper.
Step one: wash your hands.
Step two: cut the mushrooms and the garlic.
Step three: mix the eggs with a little salt and pepper.
Step four: heat the oil in a pan.
Step five: fry the rice, the garlic, and the mushrooms.
Step six: add the eggs and mix, and put a slice of chili on top.
"How much oil do we need?" I asked Chef Lucy.
"Three spoons," she said.
"How many people can eat this dish?" asked Mia.
"Six," said Chef Lucy, "and the recipe is easy."
